summary: US-F4: The settlement ledger attributes every fee cent to a payee
description:
**As** a platform operator, **I want** a captured order to land as ledger entries that name every
payee and account for every cent, **so that** settlement is a read of recorded fact rather than a
recomputation.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-215, TKT-216

The other half of TKT-6's second COS: *the settlement ledger attributes every fee cent to a payee;
splits sum exactly to totals*. ADR-002 puts the settlement ledger in `payments`, next to the
append-only money journal.

**Two traps worth naming up front.** First, **absorbed fees still have to balance**: the buyer paid
face value, the payee is owed a fee out of it, so the organizer's line is face value *minus* the
absorbed fee. A ledger that only records passed-on fees balances against the charge and is wrong
about who earned what. Second, **capture is replayed** — ADR-016's recovery path re-runs a
checkout that may already have captured, so entry writing is idempotent or the ledger double-counts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A migration adds settlement entries to payments: scoped to the organizer and the captured
  order/fact, naming the payee, an entry kind (face value vs fee), the fee code where applicable,
  amount and currency. **Append-only**, enforced the same way `journal_entries` enforces it — a
  trigger that raises on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE.
- [ ] Entries are written **in the same transaction** as the capture's journal append (ADR-003 /
  ADR-011). A capture that journals but does not settle, or settles twice, is not a state this
  system can reach.
- [ ] **Sum-exactness is proven, not asserted in prose**: for a captured order, the entries sum
  exactly to the captured amount. A test constructs a deliberately unbalanced set and shows it is
  refused. State plainly — and test — whether the refusal is a database constraint or an
  application check, and why that is the right level.
- [ ] Absorbed fees are recorded as a payee credit against a reduced organizer line, so the buyer's
  total is untouched **and** the ledger still balances. A test asserts both halves at once: same
  captured amount, different entry set, exact sum.
- [ ] Idempotent under replay: re-running a capture that already settled writes nothing new and
  changes no amount (ADR-016's recovery path is the fixture, not a hand-rolled second call).
- [ ] The entries for an order are readable through a contract-declared internal response; regen
  committed.
- [ ] The integrity claim **names its adversary** (ADR-021). Either the entries join the journal's
  hash chain and the claim is tamper-evidence, or they do not and the claim is honest-writer
  consistency. Say which, in the ADR/ledger comment, in the words ADR-021 uses. Do not write
  "tamper-evident" about state a database writer can edit.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code committed before the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** settlement reports, per-event rollups and exports (TKT-23) · payout execution
(not in this epic) · fee/settlement reversal on refund, exchange and cancellation (carved out to a
follow-up; see the epic readiness verdict) · the back-office settlement page (TKT-23 owns it, and
ADR-042 records that its route must be added to the role matrix when it lands).

objective.note: Every captured cent is attributed to a payee in an append-only ledger, and the attribution is provably exact.

scope.note: Payments: schema + write at capture + one internal read. Commerce hands over the resolved split it already computed; it does not re-resolve.

uncertainties.note: Whether the split travels on the existing charge call or a separate internal call, and whether entries chain into the journal hash (which decides the ADR-021 wording). Both are plan-stage calls; the ACs constrain either answer.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-215 (the breakdown to settle) and TKT-216 (the allocator that turns it into payee parts).

approach.note: Follow journal_entries: append-only trigger, organizer scoping, one transaction with the money fact. The recovery runner is the replay fixture.

first_slice.note: Last slice - it consumes both predecessors and is the COS's visible end.

success.note: Exact-sum, refusal and idempotency assertions, all deterministic.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

governingAdrs.why: SHIPPED BY TKT-216 AND THIS TICKET'S DIRECT INPUT. The allocator (services/payments/internal/splits.Allocate) is already written and tested: largest remainder, exact sum, ties on payee id, never forms amount*share_bps, and VALIDATES ITS OWN INPUT because this ticket hands it persisted snapshots. §5 records two integrity escapes review found in the balance triggers - a moved part validating only its destination, and TRUNCATE firing no row trigger - so do not assume a stored schedule is balanced; the allocator re-checks and so must you.

The fee model. §2: a resolved fee of amount 0 is STILL a fee and must appear - so a payee can legitimately be owed zero, and that is different from absent. §3: incidence decides who bears it, and an ABSORBED fee is still owed to a payee out of money the buyer already paid, which is the case most likely to be got wrong here.

Every money mutation flows through the append-only journal. Settlement entries are money state and inherit that discipline - journal_entries' trigger refusing UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE is the pattern to COPY, not to reinvent (TKT-216 shipped that exact hole by writing a new guard from first principles).
The checkout journal protocol fixes what is written at capture and in which transaction. Settlement entries join that transaction or they can diverge from the money fact.

Checkout recovery REPLAYS a capture whose outcome is unknown. Entry writing must be idempotent under that replay, and the recovery runner is the fixture that proves it - not a hand-rolled second call.

Name the adversary before writing 'tamper-evident'. State inside the database cannot constrain an adversary who writes to the database. Either the entries join the journal's hash chain and the claim is tamper-evidence, or they do not and it is honest-writer consistency. Say which.
payments owns the settlement ledger. catalog owns the rules; commerce composes the money. This ticket must not move that line.
The PSP port: the captured amount is what the provider confirmed. The ledger settles THAT number, never a recomputation.
Contract-first; regen committed before the gate.
Migrations run out-of-band via each binary's migrate subcommand.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and the three epic-level COS
THE ALLOCATOR IS ALREADY BUILT - use it, do not rewrite it
The append-only pattern to copy verbatim, including the TRUNCATE guard

What commerce persists and this ticket settles from: {resolution, breakdown, face_value, passed_on_fees, absorbed_fees, total_amount}; breakdown items are {fee_code, basis, incidence, amount, currency}; the resolution carries each code's split with payee parts
The capture path and its idempotency registry

TKT-215 closeout: refunds under-refund by the passed-on fee, and the fee-on-exchange policy was decided by an agent as 'carried'. Both are things this ledger will eventually have to reverse and neither is decided
TKT-216 closeout: two integrity escapes got through a deferred-trigger design; distrust 'the database enforces it' without reading how far it goes

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-217 (US-F4)

**Selection.** The last child of TKT-6, and now the only claimable one. Both blockers closed.

**Blockers verified:** `blocked-by TKT-215` — resolved (`f1d5f44f`). `blocked-by TKT-216` — resolved
(`43fdd0f5`). Zero open.

**Branch:** `TKT-217-settlement-ledger`, cut from `origin/main` at `ac550399`.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.** This ticket writes the ledger that says who is owed what.
It touches the capture transaction, adds append-only money state, and makes an integrity claim. Money
path, data migration, and an audit-trail assertion all apply — this is the highest-risk ticket of the
four, and it is the one whose mistakes are least recoverable: a misattributed cent stays
misattributed.

**Gates waived — same terms as TKT-214/215/216**, restated so this ticket stands alone: Gate 1 by the
owner's instruction; Gate 2 by agent judgement after the cross-model critique; Gate 3 by agent
squash-merge after the ai-review converges under the churn cap, review-guide first; Gate 4 by
self-validation against test evidence on merged code.

**Model routing** re-read at claim, unchanged: `plan` = `gpt-5.6-luna` · `planReview` = `main-agent` ·
`implement` = `main-agent` · `aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-luna`.

**Context-mémo re-baked**, and this one carries more than ADRs:

- **ADR-047 leads** — the allocator is **already written and tested**. This ticket consumes
  `splits.Allocate`; it does not reimplement it.
- **ADR-003 flagged with a specific instruction**: copy `journal_entries`' append-only trigger,
  including its TRUNCATE guard. TKT-216 shipped exactly that hole by writing a new guard from first
  principles while the battle-tested one sat in this same service. That is the "prior art" retro item
  from TKT-216, applied to the next ticket rather than filed and forgotten.
- **Both predecessors' closeouts are references**, because they carry facts no code shows: refunds
  currently under-refund by the passed-on fee, the fee-on-exchange policy was chosen by an agent as
  "carried", and a deferred-trigger design had two escapes. All three bear on what this ledger must
  eventually reverse.

**Applying TKT-216's process wins:** the `agent:plan-review` label moves **before** the critique, and
I will run `golangci-lint` plus every module's tests before invoking the gate.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — TKT-217 (draft)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex, read-only, effort=high)**, per `config.models.plan`. Condensed.

#### 1. Entry model and arithmetic

`payments.settlement_entries`, one immutable row per line: organizer, order, `capture_fact_id`,
account role (`organizer`|`payee`), payee identity **snapshotted** so later catalog edits cannot
change historical settlement, `entry_kind` (`face_value`|`fee`), `fee_code` + `incidence` on fee
rows, amount, currency.

    organizer face entry = F − A
    fee entries          = allocated parts of every fee
    sum = (F − A) + P + A = F + P = C

Worked: face 5000, passed-on 600, absorbed 400, captured 5600 → organizer 4600 · venue/booking 360 ·
artist/booking 240 · system/service (absorbed) 400 · **total 5600**.

Uses the existing `splits.Allocate`; includes zero-valued parts (ADR-046 §2). *"Reject if `A > F`,
`C != snapshot.total_amount`, currencies differ, or any fee cannot be allocated."*

#### 2. Boundary and transaction

catalog resolves · commerce composes and persists the snapshot · **payments allocates and owns the
ledger**. Commerce sends a contract-declared settlement projection **derived from the persisted
snapshot, never a fresh catalog read**.

The draft then proposes restructuring capture: validate+allocate before the PSP, persist the plan on
`payment_operations`, and one transaction that locks the operation, appends `payment.captured`,
inserts entries and completes the operation — *"introduce a transaction-aware capture/finalization
method rather than composing independent calls"*, because `Journal.Append` owns its own transaction
and the handler appends before `CompleteOperation`.

#### 3. Sum-exactness at two levels

Application validation before any PSP call (catches `ErrUnbalanced`, `unsplit`, currency mismatch,
provider-amount mismatch) **and** a deferred constraint trigger validating the whole set at commit
(catches missing/extra rows, direct SQL, and application bugs that bypass the builder). *"A per-row
CHECK cannot validate a set sum."* Aggregate in `numeric` to avoid a `bigint` sum overflow. Copy the
append-only pattern from `0001_journal.sql` **including the statement-level TRUNCATE trigger**.

#### 4. Replay

Adds a provider-neutral `FinalizeCapture` to the recovery payments port and HTTP client, called from
the charge path, on replay, in `confirmation_pending` recovery, and after `payment_unknown` resolves.
Idempotent: matching rows → no writes; missing rows → repair only if the stored plan matches;
conflicting plan → fail closed; never a second PSP call.

#### 5. Integrity claim

**Do not** add settlement rows to the journal hash chain in this ticket. The claim is
**honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence** — an adversary with payments DB access can drop
triggers. Record it in a new ADR; never describe the entries as tamper-evident.

#### 6–9. DoD, files, tests

ADR-048 · payments migration `0004` · store/api/settlement changes · **PSP port + fake + Stripe
adapter** for a provider-confirmed captured amount · commerce `server.go`, `recovery/runner.go`,
`recovery/clients.go` · five smoke files.

Tests to observe failing first: absorbed-fee entry build (organizer 4600, fees 1000, total 5600) ·
unbalanced persisted split refused **before the PSP**, asserting no PSP call, no journal row, no
settlement row · unbalanced set refused at commit, with a fixture whose *only* failing condition is
the balance trigger · append-only UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE each separately · zero fee still names every
payee · `unsplit` fails closed · provider-amount mismatch fails closed · recovery finalizes before
confirm · replay of a settled capture is a no-op.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Adversarial plan critique — TKT-217

**By `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**, per `config.models.planReview`. Label moved **before** the
critique began, per TKT-215's retro.

#### Seam verification at HEAD — clean

`splits.Allocate` · `0001_journal.sql`'s two triggers · `0014_fee_composition.sql`'s envelope ·
`catalog_fees.go` · `payment_operations` · `recovery/runner.go` · the charge handler — **all exist as
described.** The arithmetic is correct: I derived `(F−A)+P+A = F+P = C` independently before reading
the draft and it matches, worked example included.

#### ⛔ A1 [blocking] — the capture-flow restructure, the PSP port change, `FinalizeCapture` and the
recovery changes are all unnecessary. Delete them.

The draft's §2 and §4 exist to guarantee "a capture that journals but does not settle is unreachable"
and "replay writes nothing new". **Both are already true for free**, and the evidence is in the code
it cited:

- **`payment.captured` is appended in exactly ONE place** — `api/server.go:265`. I grepped every
  append site.
- **The fact id is deterministic**: `uuid.NewSHA1(… "payment:"+org+":"+key+":"+factType)`
  (`server.go:264`).
- **`Journal.Append` already owns a transaction and is already idempotent on that id**:
  `store.go:163-168` loads the existing fact and returns `(existing, replay=true, commit)` **without
  writing**, and re-checks under the organizer lock at `:182-188` so a concurrent identical append is
  a clean replay rather than a PK violation.

So: **write the settlement entries inside `Append`'s existing transaction, immediately after the
journal insert.** Then entries exist **iff** the captured fact exists — one transaction, one writer,
no new state machine. Replay hits the existing-fact branch and writes nothing, which is AC 5 by
construction rather than by a new endpoint.

What the draft proposes instead: a new provider-neutral HTTP operation, a new PSP port method, a
restructured capture flow, and changes to the recovery runner and its client — **on the capture
path**, which is the most sensitive code in this system, to solve a problem the deterministic fact id
already solved. That is a large, risky diff bought for nothing.

*The one thing §4 is right about:* the deferred trigger on inserting a `payment.captured` fact also
constrains the generic `/internal/facts` endpoint, which allowlists that type (`store.go:129`). That
is **correct, not a side effect** — a captured fact with no settlement is precisely the state we are
forbidding, wherever it originates.

#### ⛔ A2 [blocking] — do not reject `A > F`; record the negative organizer line

*"Reject if `A > F`"* makes a **payout misconfiguration refuse a sale**, checked before the PSP call.
That is the same trade I rejected on TKT-216 and for the same reason: the buyer's purchase does not
depend on who gets paid afterwards.

It is also arithmetically unnecessary. `(F−A)+P+A = F+P = C` holds **for any A**, including `A > F`;
I verified it (face 100, absorbed 400 → organizer −300, sum still equals the captured 100). A
negative organizer line is **true**: the organizer absorbed more than they earned. A ledger's job is
to be true, not to police configuration — and reporting is where that shows up (TKT-23).

**Amendment:** allow a signed organizer entry, `CHECK` fee entries non-negative, and record the
condition. Adding a refusal later is easy; un-blocking sales after the fact is not.

#### A3 [minor] — the provider-confirmed amount is not available, and expanding scope to get it is
a different ticket

The draft wants the ledger to settle a provider-confirmed number. Today there is none:
`server.go:246` sets `prov.AuthorizedAmount, prov.CapturedAmount = in.Amount, in.Amount` — the
**request** amount. Changing the PSP port to return a confirmed amount is a real improvement and
squarely TKT-168's ("Payments exposes no provider-neutral amount evidence", already in Backlog).

**For this ticket:** settle `in.Amount`, and assert `snapshot.total_amount == in.Amount` so commerce
and payments cannot disagree about what was charged. State the residual rather than growing the diff
into another ticket's scope.

#### Accepted

The entry model and its arithmetic, including snapshotted payee identity · using `splits.Allocate`
rather than reimplementing · zero-valued parts retained · **both** validation levels, with the
draft's own reasoning that a per-row CHECK cannot see a set · the deferred set-balance trigger ·
copying `0001_journal.sql`'s append-only **and TRUNCATE** triggers · `numeric` aggregation ·
honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence · ADR-048 · the fixture obligations, especially that
the unbalanced-set fixture must fail for the *right* reason.

#### Rejected

§2's capture restructure, §4's `FinalizeCapture` and recovery changes, the PSP port change, and
`A > F` as a refusal.

#### Pre-mortem

*Assume the PR bounced.* (1) A capture succeeds and settlement is missing → the same-transaction
write plus the deferred trigger, **A1**. (2) A sale is refused because a payee is misconfigured →
**A2**. (3) The diff is too large to review on the money path → A1 removes four files and two
services from it. (4) A replay double-writes → the deterministic fact id, proven at `store.go:163`.
(5) A gate run is lost to lint or a registry test → module tests **and** `golangci-lint` before the
gate.

Lens changed the plan in three places (A1, A2, A3).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan final — TKT-217

**The `kind=plan` draft, as amended, is the plan.** Delta only.

#### Amendments

**A1** Settlement entries are written **inside `Journal.Append`'s existing transaction**. No
`FinalizeCapture`, no PSP port change, no recovery-runner change, no capture restructure — the
deterministic fact id already makes replay a no-op.
**A2** A negative organizer line is recorded, not refused. `A > F` is a true state, and payout
configuration must not refuse a sale.
**A3** Settle `in.Amount` and assert it equals `snapshot.total_amount`; the provider-confirmed
amount is TKT-168's.

#### Decisions made by the agent because Gate 2 is waived

| # | Decision | Rule | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Entries written in `Append`'s transaction | critique recommends | Entries exist iff the captured fact exists, with no new state machine on the capture path |
| D2 | Deferred trigger requires settlement for any `payment.captured` insert | critique recommends | Makes the invariant true wherever the fact comes from, including `/internal/facts` |
| D3 | Negative organizer line allowed and recorded | most reversible | The identity holds for any A; refusing couples the sale to payout config |
| D4 | Payee identity snapshotted onto the entry | critique accepts draft | A later catalog edit must not rewrite historical settlement — the discipline 0006/0014 already established |
| D5 | Honest-writer consistency, **not** tamper-evidence; no hash chain | critique accepts draft | ADR-021: DB-resident state cannot constrain a DB writer. Joining the chain is a real option and is named as future work, not claimed |
| D6 | Settle the request amount, assert it matches the snapshot | most reversible | No provider-confirmed number exists today; TKT-168 owns creating one |

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

**A1, A2, A3.** A1 is the consequential one: it **removes** a large amount of proposed work on the
capture path. If that judgement is wrong, the failure mode is a captured fact whose settlement is
missing — which is exactly what D2's deferred trigger makes impossible to commit, so the mistake
would be loud rather than silent.

#### Test seam

The pure entry builder (`face`, `passed_on`, `absorbed`, breakdown, splits → entries) beside the
allocator, plus the deferred trigger at the database. Both are the seams the previous three tickets
established.

#### Gate 2

Waived. Proceeding to `Building` with six decisions and three unreviewed amendments named.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### Implementation summary — TKT-217

**By `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**, per `config.models.implement`. PR
[#177](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/177) · 6 commits · 18 files · +1853/−15 ·
local gate **green** on the tip.

#### What shipped

`payments.settlement_entries` (migration `0004`), written **inside `Journal.Append`'s existing
transaction**, so entries exist **iff** the captured fact exists. The identity
`(F−A)+P+A = F+P = C` is enforced at two levels: the pure builder `BuildSettlementEntries`, and a
**deferred constraint trigger** over the set — plus `capture_must_settle` in the other direction,
refusing a `payment.captured` fact with no settlement, `/internal/facts` included.
ADR-048 records it. Read surface: `GET /internal/orders/{orderId}/settlement`.

#### TDD — every test observed red first

| Test | Red because |
|---|---|
| absorbed-fee build | organizer line was `F`, not `F−A` |
| negative organizer line | builder refused `A > F` |
| unattributed fee | builder refused a fee with no schedule |
| balance trigger | set summed to less than the capture and committed |
| capture-without-settlement | a bare captured fact committed |
| UPDATE / DELETE / TRUNCATE | each mutated the ledger |
| end-to-end ledger read | the operation did not exist |

**Mutation-checked**, and the procedure held this time: `go vet` the mutant *before* reading the
result. On TKT-215 and again on TKT-216 a mutation reported "no failure" because it **did not
compile** — a mutation that does not compile is not a check.

The unsplit-fee check was **blind** when first written: it passed against a mutant that dropped the
attribution entirely. Fixture widened until it could tell the difference.

#### Four defects the gate found, not review

1. **Refusing unsplit fees would have broken shipped sales.** TKT-215 shipped fees before TKT-216
   shipped schedules; every fee sold in that window has no schedule, so the refusal failed those
   sales **at checkout, after the buyer committed**. Now recorded as *collected and unattributed* —
   balanced **and** queryable, which is what an operator needs.
2. **The exchange delta charge had no attribution** → `502 exchange settlement unresolved`. TKT-215
   decided fees are *carried* on exchange, so the delta charge sends a fee-free plan.
3. **Test facts signed with an unknown key id** — `verify-journal` scans the whole table, a trap
   `journal_smoke_test.go` documents in as many words. Switched to the shared ring.
4. **The new read operation had no smoke happy-path.** Closed on the fee-incidence test that already
   drives a real sale, which is the better home anyway: the epic's headline claim is now asserted
   **through the running stack**, not at a seam.

Plus one consequence of the design itself: the ledger's foreign key to `journal_entries` makes
`TRUNCATE` illegal on the referenced table, which broke the journal tamper harness's restore.
Restores by `DELETE` now, with `DISABLE TRIGGER ALL` rather than `USER` — the append-only triggers
are user triggers, but the referential integrity blocking the delete is a system trigger.

#### Deviations from the plan-final

**None.** A1/A2/A3 held. A1 is worth marking as vindicated: the draft's `FinalizeCapture`, PSP port
change and recovery-runner changes were deleted on the argument that the deterministic fact id
already makes replay a no-op — nothing in implementation needed them back.

#### Residuals, stated not hidden

- Settles `in.Amount`, asserted equal to the snapshot total. No provider-confirmed amount exists
  today — **TKT-168** owns creating one.
- **Honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence.** Not in the hash chain; a payments-DB writer
  can drop the triggers. Named in ADR-048 §5 as future work, not claimed.

Next: `agent:ai-review` — adversarial review by `gpt-5.6-luna`, per `config.models.aiReview`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### Adversarial review — TKT-217

**Five passes by `gpt-5.6-luna`** (Codex), per `config.models.aiReview`. `implement` = `main-agent`,
so the cross-model invariant holds. **Nine findings, all fixed. Fifth pass: `approve`, no material
findings.**

| Pass | Findings | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | critical, high, high, medium |
| 2 | 2 | critical, high |
| 3 | 3 | high, high, medium |
| 4 | 1 | high |
| 5 | 0 | **approve** |

**Two of the nine were defects a previous pass's fix created.** Pass 2 found that moving plan
validation ahead of the provider left it behind `BindOperation`; pass 3 found that moving it ahead
of the lookup made idempotency depend on the plan. This is the failure mode AGENTS.md names, arrived
at three times in one ticket — a round of review fixes needs a review of the fixes' *interaction*.

#### The ordering, revised four times

`validate after PSP` → money captured, no fact, no ledger.
`validate after Bind` → recoverable operation with no usable ledger.
`validate before lookup` → idempotency depended on the plan.
**`fingerprint → lookup → validate → bind → PSP`** → converged.

#### Triage note: one diagnosis was wrong, its remedy still right

Pass 3 called the operation-count test a false positive because it "checks a different database".
That is incorrect — both handles use the same DSN, so committed rows are visible. But the test had
**no positive control**: a query observing nothing would read as "no operation survived". A control
was added for that reason, stated as such.

#### One finding escalated beyond this ticket, then came back

Pass 4's finding needed a schema and capture-path state-machine change — the work plan-final **A1
removed as unnecessary** — so it was filed as **TKT-219** and the run **stopped and reported** under
the owner's stop conditions (b) and (c). The owner directed "fix it here"; TKT-219 is now **Done**
inside this branch, and ADR-048 §3e reads as built rather than as a gap.

#### Churn

Four fix commits, each gated. One gate run (`gate217i`) was wasted by starting it and then editing
the tree — the results that count ran on frozen trees.

Review guide posted on PR [#177](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/177).

<!-- sdlc:stage=po-review kind=summary -->
### PO validation — TKT-217

Self-validated against test evidence on the **merged** code (`1ba90a4b`), Gate 4 waived for this
run. Post-merge `make check` on `main`: **green (EXIT=0)**.

| # | COS | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Migration adds settlement entries, append-only on UPDATE/DELETE/**TRUNCATE** | `0004_settlement_ledger.sql`; `TestSettlementEntriesAreAppendOnly` exercises all three separately | ✅ |
| 2 | Written in the **same transaction** as the capture's journal append | Entries inserted inside `AppendWithSettlement`'s transaction; `TestCaptureAndSettlementCommitTogether`, `TestCapturedFactWithoutSettlementCannotCommit` | ✅ |
| 3 | Sum-exactness **proven**, unbalanced set refused, level stated and justified | `TestUnbalancedSettlementSetIsRefusedAtCommit`; both levels, and ADR-048 §3 says why a per-row CHECK cannot see a set | ✅ |
| 4 | Absorbed fees: reduced organizer line, buyer's total untouched, still balances | `TestSettleFromAPlanBalances` + the builder cases: same captured 5600, different entry set, exact sum | ✅ |
| 5 | Idempotent under replay, **ADR-016's recovery path as the fixture** | `TestReplayedCaptureWritesNoSecondLedger` — see the honest note below | ⚠️ **met differently** |
| 6 | Entries readable through a contract-declared internal response; regen committed | `GET /internal/orders/{orderId}/settlement`; asserted **through the running stack** in `smoke/checkout_test.go` after a real fee-carrying sale | ✅ |

#### COS 5 — met, but not by the fixture the wording asks for

The AC names ADR-016's recovery path as the replay fixture. **That fixture does not exist**, and the
reason is structural rather than an omission: the recovery runner never re-calls `/internal/charges`
— it reads PSP status and goes to `confirmAndComplete`. There is no path by which recovery re-drives
a capture into the settlement writer.

Replay is instead proven where it actually happens: the fact id is deterministic
(`uuid.NewSHA1`), `Append` returns the existing fact without writing, and
`TestReplayedCaptureWritesNoSecondLedger` asserts no second ledger. **TKT-219** then closed the case
the AC's wording was reaching for — a retry that *isn't* a clean replay (expired lease, different
plan) can no longer re-attribute captured money.

Recording this as **met differently** rather than met: the property holds, the named fixture does
not exist, and an operator reading the AC later should know which.
